overview.headline: Random mating and assortative mating effects on Hardy Weinberg equilibrium in humans

keyPoints.point: Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium requires random mating that does not always occur in humans
keyPoints.quote: One reason that Hardy-Weinberg does not always apply to humans is that random mating, a condition of HWE (Hardy-Weinberg Equilibrium), does not occur.

keyPoints.point: Random mating implies mating should be arbitrary with regard to the locus considered
keyPoints.quote: Random mating implies that mating should be arbitrary with regard to the locus being considered.

keyPoints.point: Positive assortative mating leads to an increase in homozygotes for similar visible traits
keyPoints.quote: Positive assortative mating leads to an increase in homozygotes whereas negative assortative mating leads to an increase in heterozygotes.

keyPoints.point: Negative assortative mating is breeding between dissimilar genotypes and is more rare
keyPoints.quote: In contrast, negative assortative mating is breeding between individuals with dissimilar genotypes, and is more rare.

keyPoints.point: Assortative mating is never complete and humans mate randomly for blood type and short tandem repeat genotype
keyPoints.quote: they mate randomly with respect to other traits such as blood type and short tandem repeat (STR) genotype.

keyTerms.gloss: mating that is arbitrary with regard to the locus
keyTerms.quote: Random mating implies that mating should be arbitrary with regard to the locus being considered.

keyTerms.gloss: non-random mating between similar individuals that is positive
keyTerms.quote: This constitutes non-random, positive assortative mating.

keyTerms.gloss: breeding between dissimilar genotypes that is more rare
keyTerms.quote: In contrast, negative assortative mating is breeding between individuals with dissimilar genotypes, and is more rare.

keyTerms.gloss: individuals with identical alleles that show increase in homozygotes
keyTerms.quote: Positive assortative mating leads to an increase in homozygotes whereas negative assortative mating leads to an increase in heterozygotes.

keyTerms.gloss: individuals with different alleles that show increase in heterozygotes
keyTerms.quote: Positive assortative mating leads to an increase in homozygotes whereas negative assortative mating leads to an increase in heterozygotes.

keyTerms.gloss: genomic position that is arbitrary with regard to mating
keyTerms.quote: Random mating implies that mating should be arbitrary with regard to the locus being considered.

keyTerms.gloss: trait that mates randomly along with short tandem repeat genotype
keyTerms.quote: they mate randomly with respect to other traits such as blood type and short tandem repeat (STR) genotype.
